## What I found
- `app-pv` was pre-created and `Available`: 1Gi, `ReadWriteOnce`, `storageClassName: manual`, `hostPath: /tmp/app-pv`, reclaim policy `Retain`.
- The cluster's **default** StorageClass is `standard` (rancher.io/local-path, `WaitForFirstConsumer`). A PVC created without an explicit class would have taken `standard` and dynamically provisioned a *new* volume instead of binding `app-pv` — that was the key constraint to respect.

## Change made
Applied one manifest (`/tmp/work/app.yaml`):
- **PVC `app-pvc`**: `storageClassName: manual` (so it matches the PV, not the default class), `volumeName: app-pv` (explicit binding), `ReadWriteOnce`, request `1Gi` — exactly matching the PV's mode/capacity, so no provisioning and no resizing of the PV.
- **Pod `app`**: `image: nginx:1.31.5`, volume `appdata` → `persistentVolumeClaim.claimName: app-pvc`, mounted at `mountPath: /data`.

The PV's own spec was left untouched (capacity, class, reclaim policy, hostPath all unchanged), and no other cluster objects were modified.

| Check | Observed value |
|---|---|
| PVC bound to the pre-created PV | `status.phase=Bound`, `spec.volumeName=app-pv` |
| PV consumed by this claim | `app-pv` status `Bound`, `claim=default/app-pvc` |
| Storage class match | PVC `manual` / PV `manual` |
| Pod running the intended image | `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` (container `Ready=True`, `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts) |
| Claim mounted at `/data` | `volumeMounts[0].mountPath=/data` → volume backed by PVC `app-pvc` |
| `/data` is really the PV, data persists | Wrote `/data/probe.txt` in the pod; a temporary pod mounting `hostPath: /tmp/app-pv` read back `hello-from-app`; `df /data` showed the node's tmpfs, distinct from the container rootfs |
| No side effects | `pv-reader` helper pod deleted; 10 cluster pods (9 system + `app`), nothing else altered |

Done. Both objects are created and verified.

## What I found
- `app-pv` was pre-created and `Available`: 1Gi, `ReadWriteOnce`, `storageClassName: manual`, `hostPath: /tmp/app-pv`, reclaim policy `Retain`.
- The cluster's **default** StorageClass is `standard` (rancher.io/local-path, `WaitForFirstConsumer`). A PVC created without an explicit class would have taken `standard` and dynamically provisioned a *new* volume instead of binding `app-pv` — that was the key constraint to respect.

## Change made
Applied one manifest (`/tmp/work/app.yaml`):
- **PVC `app-pvc`**: `storageClassName: manual` (so it matches the PV, not the default class), `volumeName: app-pv` (explicit binding), `ReadWriteOnce`, request `1Gi` — exactly matching the PV's mode/capacity, so no provisioning and no resizing of the PV.
- **Pod `app`**: `image: nginx:1.31.5`, volume `appdata` → `persistentVolumeClaim.claimName: app-pvc`, mounted at `mountPath: /data`.

The PV's own spec was left untouched (capacity, class, reclaim policy, hostPath all unchanged), and no other cluster objects were modified.

## Verification (direct observations)
| Check | Observed value |
|---|---|
| PVC bound to the pre-created PV | `status.phase=Bound`, `spec.volumeName=app-pv` |
| PV consumed by this claim | `app-pv` status `Bound`, `claim=default/app-pvc` |
| Storage class match | PVC `manual` / PV `manual` |
| Pod running the intended image | `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` (container `Ready=True`, `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts) |
| Claim mounted at `/data` | `volumeMounts[0].mountPath=/data` → volume backed by PVC `app-pvc` |
| `/data` is really the PV, data persists | Wrote `/data/probe.txt` in the pod; a temporary pod mounting `hostPath: /tmp/app-pv` read back `hello-from-app`; `df /data` showed the node's tmpfs, distinct from the container rootfs |
| No side effects | `pv-reader` helper pod deleted; 10 cluster pods (9 system + `app`), nothing else altered |

One transient `FailedScheduling: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims` event appeared in the first second while the binder completed; it resolved immediately and was followed by `Scheduled` → `Pulled` → `Started`, so no action was needed.
